h1: AI Product Videos for Electronics, From Unboxing to Everyday Use
lead: Turn one clear product photo into electronics video ads that show a useful feature, a quick setup, or a product in daily use.
card: What's in the box, scale in a hand and gadgets in everyday use.
intro: AI product videos for electronics can use a context scene to show where a device fits: earbuds on a run, a power bank in a carry-on, or a ring light at a desk. Keep verified specifications in the listing and use separate photos to show physical details.

Upload a clear shot of your product with its ports, buttons, and indicator lights visible, then describe what should happen: a lid lifting off the box, a cable clicking into place, a speaker sitting on a picnic blanket at sunset. Choose a 6-, 10-, or 15-second clip for the product moment. Battery life, wattage, and other specs belong in the text you add yourself, where you control the exact figures. For gallery photos, photograph the front, side and back so every detail shown comes from a real upload.

ideas.d: Put a mechanical keyboard on a tidy desk, a fitness tracker on a wrist mid-workout, or a mini projector lighting up a bedroom wall. Context tells a shopper who the product is for faster than a spec sheet does.
A slow turn on a dark surface with a single edge light suits headphones, speakers, and chargers. Use it for launch posts and at the top of a product page.
For Black Friday or back-to-school, generate a clean clip of the device first, then add the price and the deal's end date in Ads Manager or CapCut, where you control every digit.

faq.q: Can the video show my charger plugged into a well-known phone brand?
faq.a: Another company's logo or trademark can get a request declined, so describe a generic device instead, like "a black smartphone on a nightstand." The scene still makes the use clear.

faq.q: Can the screen in the video show my app or interface?
faq.a: On-screen text and app layouts tend to come out garbled. Ask for a dark screen or a soft glow instead, then place real screenshots over it in CapCut or Canva.

faq.q: Which video size should I use for an Amazon or Shopify product page?
faq.a: 16:9 is the usual choice for a video on a product page, and 1:1 also sits well in a listing gallery. Choose 9:16 if the same clip will run on TikTok or YouTube Shorts.

faq.q: My glossy device shows glare and fingerprints. How do I fix that?
faq.a: Wipe off dust and fingerprints, peel away any shipping film, and shoot at a slight angle so the device's depth shows. Switch off overhead lights that leave hot spots on glossy cases.

faq.q: What should a product video for electronics show?
faq.a: Show one real action: a button press, a port close-up, a device being unboxed, or a hand placing it next to a generic laptop or phone. Avoid naming another brand and keep the scene focused on how your device works.

faq.q: Can I make an unboxing video without filming it myself?
faq.a: Yes. Upload a clear photo of the product and choose an unboxing format; adult hands can lift the item from a plain box and hold it in view. The generated video keeps the device shape, ports and color from your photo.

faq.q: Which size works for product pages versus feed ads?
faq.a: Use a square 1:1 video or photo for Amazon, Shopify and most product carousels, and a vertical 9:16 video for TikTok, Reels, Shorts and other in-feed placements. The format selector shows both before you run the job.

overview.h2: Show the device before you explain the specs

items.d: A front, side, and back source can establish ports, buttons, indicator lights, finish, and included pieces. Use the generated scene to explain where the device belongs in a day, not to replace a specification sheet.

Unbox, place, clip, plug, carry, or set the device down. One clear action gives a short clip structure; keep battery life, wattage, compatibility, and interface screenshots with the verified details on your product listing.
Photograph the front, back, and sides of the device. Include ports, buttons, vents, lens rings, or indicator lights that a scene may reveal.
Lay out the device, cable, adapter, case, manual, and retail box when an unboxing result should show what arrives.
Wipe fingerprints and use side light rather than a hard overhead source. A small rotation can keep glare from covering a control or logo.
Keep the uploaded screen dark or simple if text matters. Plan to place an approved screenshot over it after download instead of trusting generated interface lettering.
Name a desk, carry-on, locker bench, or nightstand and avoid another company's logo unless you have permission to show it.
